items.text: If unable to stop on runway:

sections.title: EMERGENCY LANDING PATTERN
sections.condition: TO BE USED FOR: -- ENGINE FAILURE OR MALFUNCTION -- PRECAUTIONARY EMERGENCY LANDING -- SIMULATED ENGINE FAILURE

items.text: 90 KIAS over intended point of landing. Turn to Low Key.

items.detail: unprepared surfaces or water. Maintain 90 KIAS.

items.text: 85 KIAS (gear down), 90 KIAS (gear up), wingtip distance abeam intended point of landing.

sections.title: LOW ALTITUDE ENGINE FAILURE
sections.condition: If engine fails at or below 1000 feet AGL:

items.text:
Assume safe gliding attitude. 75 KIAS  FLAPS DOWN
                             80 KIAS   FLAPS UP
Select best available landing area and turn to intercept the emergency landing pattern at the maximum altitude practicable.
Assume safe gliding attitude. Best glide is 90 KIAS

Select best available landing area and turn to intercept the emergency landing pattern at the maximum altitude practicable. If power is available, climb to an altitude from which the aircraft can glide to a high key position.
A fire in the wing could be caused by fuel leakage and / or defective electrical wiring. Perform the following procedure:
Attempt to extinguish the fire by slipping aircraft away from fire.
If fire does not extinguish or is obviously fed by fuel
Determine source of smoke and execute appropriate emergency procedures.

sections.condition: Check fuel system for secondary indications and proceed as follows:

items.text: Utilize landing gear emergency extension system.
Accomplish landing, clear runway, secure engine, and ABANDON AIRCRAFT.
Check each necessary circuit one at a time by pushing IN circuit breaker and turning ON radio / electrical equipment it services.
Secure unnecessary radio / electrical equipment to conserve battery if generator is secured.
Adjust throttle to maintain safe flight while minimizing overspeed.
Climb to put load on propeller.
Manipulate propeller control in an attempt to restore governing.

items.detail: (if warning light is on or voltage exceeds 30 volts)

items.text: Know any peculiar local area procedures
If aircraft is controllable, climb to at least 5000 feet.
Communicate – state difficulty, request visual inspection.
Fly wide approach, maintaining 10 knots above minimums obtained during flight tests.
Push clutch knob DOWN to engage crank.

items.detail: (crank until handle will not move any further)

items.text: Plan to touch down before all fuel is exhausted to have power for controlled approach.

Make normal approach with power, if possible.
Approach stall attitude at a speed under which full control of aircraft can be maintained. Plan landing direction as follows:
Calm sea – Into wind
Moderate swells – Parallel to swells
High swells (25 knots of wind or more) – Into wind, attempting to land on upwind side of swell.
Release safety belt ONLY after aircraft has come to a full stop.
If the gear cannot be lowered successfully, proceed with the following emergency procedures for the appropriate gear malfunction.
If an unsafe gear indication existed and the gear have been successfully lowered, do not attempt to raise the gear. Raising the gear after a malfunction could cause further damage.
ABANDON AIRCRAFT as soon as it stops.
Reduce airspeed: lower gear and flaps.
Make gentle pitching oscillations (use centrifugal force to swing nose gear into down position).
When landing, lower nosewheel to runway gently.
Use forward stick to keep nosewheel firmly on runway. Avoid wheel barrowing.
After touching main wheels down, hold nose up as long as possible with full nose down elevator trim and full backstick.
ABANDON AIRCRAFT as soon as it stops.
Have gear position checked visually by another pilot or by the tower on a flyby, if possible.

If verified that one gear is not fully extended and an attempt to retract it is unsuccessful, execute normal approach with full flaps and power on to reduce landing speed, carrying the wing slightly lower on the down and locked side.
Touch down smoothly on the down and locked gear. Hold opposite wing up with aileron as long as possible after nosewheel touches down.
When wingtip strikes the ground, apply maximum opposite brake pressure.
Touch down well over opposite side of runway to allow room for a swerve and hold directional control with opposite brake.
After landing with a flat tire, perform the Secure Checklist when the aircraft comes to a complete stop and have the aircraft towed clear of the landing area.
Do not taxi in with a flat tire.

If no brake pressure was evident during landing pattern brake check, land aircraft as short as possible using full flaps to shorten landing roll. After touchdown, secure the engine. When the aircraft comes to a complete stop, complete the remaining items on the Secure Checklist and have the aircraft towed clear of the landing area.
Runway permitting, execute a full stop.
Do not attempt to taxi the aircraft.
Have landing gear checked visually by another pilot or by tower on a flyby, if possible.
If the check reveals no visible damage, execute a normal full flap landing and proceed as in steps 1 and 2.
If visual damage is confirmed, execute appropriate emergency procedure.
